overview: Shenzhou International is a vertically integrated apparel manufacturer that designs fabric, dyes/finishes it, and cuts and sews garments for global brands, with production bases in mainland China, Cambodia, and Vietnam (108,680 employees, ~280,000 metric tons/year fabric capacity and ~600 million pieces/year garment capacity as of FY2025). It is the largest OEM/ODM knitwear manufacturer for sportswear brands globally, with Nike, Adidas, Uniqlo (Fast Retailing) and Puma together estimated to account for roughly 80% of revenue. The company reports in RMB, sells mostly in USD, and is listed on the HKEX main board (joined the Hang Seng Index in 2018).

business_model.summary: Shenzhou earns fees as a contract manufacturer (OEM/ODM) for global apparel brands, controlling the full value chain from yarn/fabric knitting, dyeing and finishing through garment cutting and sewing. Pricing is cost-plus/negotiated per order with no owned consumer brand, so profitability depends on factory utilization, labor productivity, raw material costs, and the USD/RMB exchange rate (sales are USD-denominated while costs are largely RMB-denominated). Revenue is order-driven/project-based rather than recurring, though relationships with core brand clients are long-term and deeply integrated (co-development of fabrics ahead of each season).

revenue_streams.name: Sportswear
revenue_streams.trend: growing (FY2025), but down double-digits in H1 FY2026

business_model.customer_type: B2B — small number of large global sportswear/apparel brands (Nike, Adidas, Uniqlo/Fast Retailing, Puma are core clients; combined estimated ~80% of revenue per third-party research, not disclosed exactly by the company)
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2025 revenue by market: Europe 20.2%, U.S. 18.0%, Japan 16.6%, Other international 21.4% (international subtotal 76.2%), China domestic 23.8%. Production footprint: mainland China, Cambodia, Vietnam, with a new garment base in Indonesia in early construction (land handed over August 2026).

competitive_position.market_position: Largest vertically-integrated knitwear manufacturer serving premium global sportswear brands; estimated mid-single-digit-to-low-teens share of the premium sportswear OEM/ODM export market, well ahead of individual peers such as Crystal International and Eclat Textile (unverified third-party estimates).

moat_factors.description: In-house fabric knitting, dyeing/finishing, printing and garment assembly gives faster turnaround, tighter quality control, and the ability to co-develop proprietary functional fabrics with brand R&D teams — a capability most garment-only CMT (cut-make-trim) competitors lack.

Multi-country base (China, Vietnam, Cambodia, soon Indonesia) lets Shenzhou offer brands tariff/geopolitical diversification and large single-order capacity that smaller regional manufacturers cannot match.
Deep, multi-year technical collaboration with core brands (fabric R&D, quality systems) creates switching friction, though brands can and do multi-source across several large manufacturers.

Scale procurement and automation investment support cost efficiency, but labor cost inflation in China and a strengthening RMB are eroding this advantage relative to Vietnam/Cambodia-based and other Southeast Asian competitors.

weaknesses: High customer concentration — four brand clients estimated at ~80% of revenue; loss of or order cuts from any one would be material
No pricing power/owned brand — a pure contract manufacturer subject to brand clients' sourcing and pricing decisions
Margins highly exposed to RMB/USD exchange rate since revenue is USD and costs are RMB
Labor-intensive model increasingly pressured by rising Chinese wages and demographic headwinds (shrinking working-age population)
New overseas capacity (Cambodia garment factory, second Vietnam fabric plant) still ramping and diluting margins during the build-out phase

growth_drivers: Continued overseas capacity expansion (Cambodia garment factory ramp, second Vietnam fabric factory, new Indonesia garment base) diversifying away from China and reducing tariff/geopolitical exposure
Deepening wallet share with existing core brand clients through new product categories (football apparel, basketball, running) and functional/eco-friendly fabrics
Domestic technology upgrades and automation (Ningbo, Anhui bases) to offset rising labor costs and improve productivity
Secular tailwind from outdoor sports, functional, and eco-friendly apparel demand globally
Selective new-customer diversification beyond the core four brands to reduce concentration risk
China domestic consumption-support policies potentially stabilizing the ~24% of revenue from the domestic market

business.description: Nike, Adidas, Uniqlo/Fast Retailing and Puma estimated at ~80% of revenue combined; order volatility or loss of any one client would be highly material to revenue and margins.
FY2025 and H1 FY2026 commentary both cite subdued brand-client restocking and cautious ordering amid high retail inventory and soft consumer spending in Europe/US/Japan.
New Cambodia garment factory and Vietnam fabric plant are still reaching normal productivity; the new Indonesia base adds further execution complexity.
Management describes an industry-wide pattern of 'strong supply and weak demand' with some competitors sacrificing margin for volume.

financial.description: Sales are USD-denominated, costs largely RMB-denominated; RMB appreciated ~4% on average in H1 FY2026 vs H1 FY2025, directly compressing gross margin (-4.5pp) and causing FX revaluation losses on USD-denominated net assets.
Gearing ratio (borrowings/equity) rose to 39.5% at FY2025/H1 FY2026 from 29.9% in FY2022, though the balance sheet remains net-cash-to-near-net-cash and liquidity is strong (current ratio ~2.2-2.3x).
Labor costs (28.1% of sales in FY2025, up from 27.6%) and synthetic fiber/polyester costs (linked to crude oil volatility from Middle East geopolitical tension) are both increasing.

regulatory.risk: US tariff policy / Section 301 and transshipment scrutiny
regulatory.description: New Section 301 tariff actions and intensified rules-of-origin/transshipment reviews continue to pressure China-origin apparel exports to the US; China's apparel import share in the US fell to ~10.7% in H1 2026 from higher levels, with Vietnam now the largest US apparel source (~21.7% share).
EU's Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation designates textiles/clothing as a first-wave category subject to new ecodesign and energy-labelling requirements, raising compliance costs.
Government plans targeting 70%+ digitalization of key processes by 2027 require continued capex in automation and ESG compliance.

macro.description: Apparel demand is discretionary and sensitive to consumer confidence in the US, Europe, and Japan — Shenzhou's three largest international markets.
China recorded its fourth consecutive year of population decline in 2025, shrinking the working-age labor pool and structurally raising domestic labor costs over time.
Middle East tensions drove crude oil and synthetic fiber cost volatility; broader trade-bloc fragmentation is forcing costly supply-chain reconfiguration.

macro.risk: Cotton and raw material price volatility
macro.description: Global cotton supply/demand and prices remain volatile, though FY2025 commentary notes relatively low absolute price levels; H1 FY2026 notes cotton prices rising.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global apparel/textile OEM industry characterized by 'strong supply, weak demand' with capacity migrating to Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Cambodia) amid US tariff and rules-of-origin pressure on China-origin goods; structural growth pockets exist in functional/outdoor/eco-friendly apparel.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — contract manufacturing volumes track global brand inventory cycles and consumer discretionary spending; H1 FY2026 showed a sharp swing from FY2025 growth to revenue decline as destocking and cautious ordering returned.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (net cash-like balance sheet with modest borrowings), but moderate indirect sensitivity via consumer discretionary spending and via PBOC/Fed rate differentials that influence RMB/USD exchange rates.
key_input_costs: RMB/USD exchange rate (effectively a major 'cost' given USD revenue/RMB cost base)

recent_developments.event: H1 FY2026 interim results: revenue fell 5.3% YoY to RMB14.18bn, gross margin fell 4.5pp to 22.6%, profit attributable to owners fell 40.0% YoY to RMB1.90bn, driven primarily by RMB appreciation against USD (~4% average appreciation) and associated FX revaluation losses, plus rising wage/retirement costs and softer brand-client ordering.
Interim dividend cut to HK$0.88 per share from HK$1.38 a year earlier (~36% reduction), reflecting the profit decline.

Land for a new garment manufacturing base in Indonesia was formally handed over to the Group; civil engineering works to commence immediately, extending geographic diversification beyond China/Vietnam/Cambodia.

Second Vietnam (Tây Ninh) fabric factory ramp-up proceeding smoothly, now at ~100 tonnes/day; Cambodia garment factory continuing to ramp staffing (~5,400 employees, ~90% of target headcount, ~85% of normal production efficiency per FY2025 report) and Anhui (China) base technological upgrade civil works completed.

US apparel sourcing mix continued shifting away from China: China's share of US apparel imports fell to ~10.7% (down ~5pp YoY, slipping to third place), while Vietnam became the largest single source at ~21.7% share — underscoring the rationale for Shenzhou's continued Vietnam/Cambodia/Indonesia capacity build-out.
UBS downgraded the stock to Neutral with a price target of HK$69 (from prior Buy rating), versus a share price of ~HK$61.50 at the time.

FY2025 annual results: revenue grew 8.1% to RMB30.99bn, but gross margin compressed 1.8pp to 26.3% and net profit fell 6.7% to RMB5.83bn (partly due to a one-off disposal gain in the FY2024 comparative base; underlying profit decline ~1.4%), as rising labor costs, US tariff cost-sharing with customers, and RMB appreciation weighed on margins even as volumes grew.

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 Interim Report (August 2026) / FY2025 Annual Report (March 2026)

items.notes: Management does not issue formal quantitative revenue or margin guidance in these filings; commentary is qualitative, emphasizing 'sustainable growth' and capacity-driven volume gains rather than a specific target.

items.target: Continue Vietnam second fabric factory ramp-up, Cambodia garment factory ramp-up, Anhui (China) technology upgrade, and new Indonesia garment base construction
items.vs_prior: maintained/expanded (Indonesia is new vs. prior year's stated plans)
items.notes: FY2025 capex was ~RMB3.00bn (42% equipment, 54% buildings/land); H1 FY2026 filing adds Indonesia as a new capacity destination, land handed over August 2026.

items.target: Qualitative: product innovation/differentiation, lean cost control, digital/automation upgrades, global production diversification, selective new-customer acquisition
items.notes: Consistent strategic framework repeated across FY2025 annual report and H1 FY2026 interim report; no new numeric KPI targets introduced.

guidance.management_commentary: Management's tone turned more cautious in the H1 FY2026 report versus the FY2025 annual report: it cites 'insufficient momentum in the recovery of end-consumer demand,' continued RMB appreciation risk, raw material cost volatility (tied to Middle East-driven oil price swings), and persistent US tariff/transshipment-scrutiny pressure as near-term headwinds, while reiterating long-term confidence in diversified global capacity and deepened brand-client relationships to 'jointly withstand cyclical pressures.'

bull_case: Industry-leading vertically integrated manufacturer with scale, quality, and speed advantages that are difficult for smaller CMT competitors to replicate
Strong, largely net-cash balance sheet (gearing 39.5%, current ratio >2x) provides resilience through the current demand downturn and funds continued overseas capacity expansion
Geographic diversification (Vietnam, Cambodia, now Indonesia) reduces China-specific tariff and labor-cost risk and positions the company to capture share as brands de-risk sourcing away from China

Valuation already reflects a cyclical trough view — trailing P/E near 10x and forward P/E below 9x (per info.json screen data) versus a company with a multi-decade track record of profitability and brand-client loyalty
Long-standing, deeply integrated relationships with top-tier global sportswear brands support demand recovery once brand-client destocking cycles normalize
bear_case: High customer concentration (~80% of revenue from four brands) leaves earnings highly exposed to any single client's sourcing decisions, demand softness, or margin negotiations

H1 FY2026 results show a sharp deterioration — revenue -5.3%, gross margin -4.5pp, profit -40% — driven by RMB appreciation, raw material cost inflation, and cautious brand-client ordering, with limited visibility on when these pressures ease

No pricing power as a pure contract manufacturer; margins are structurally squeezed between rising China/Vietnam/Cambodia labor costs and brand clients' bargaining power, compounded by RMB/USD currency mismatch (USD revenue, RMB costs)
US tariff policy and transshipment/rules-of-origin scrutiny remain an unresolved overhang on China-origin apparel exports, even as the company diversifies production out of China
Heavy ongoing capex into new/ramping capacity (Cambodia, Vietnam, Indonesia) dilutes near-term margins and carries execution risk before reaching normalized productivity
